title: Sir Arthur C. Clarke Deserves a Nobel Prize
gist: Mostly a promotional piece by Richard Curtin (Silicon Catalyst; raw author field lists Daniel Nenni) for the November 11, 2026 Silicon Catalyst Semiconductor Industry Forum 'What's Next: AI, Quantum & Space', featuring a GlobalFoundries CEO keynote, wrapped in a tongue-in-cheek case for a posthumous Nobel for Arthur C. Clarke. Substantive content is limited to the forum's thesis that AI-to-edge, quantum and space will create new semiconductor demand vectors.

themes.theme: Forum thesis: AI, quantum, space as chip demand

insights.claim: Silicon Catalyst frames AI, quantum and the space economy as a confluence driving a semiconductor transformation unlike anything since the internet and mobile computing.
insights.speaker: Richard Curtin
insights.so_what: Signals where early-stage chip startup/incubator attention is going over the next decade.
insights.locator: The semiconductor industry is approaching a period

insights.claim: The forum argues AI will push computing from centralized data centers to edge devices, autonomous systems, robotics and physical AI, driving demand for compute, memory, connectivity, sensing, photonics and power efficiency.
insights.speaker: Richard Curtin
insights.so_what: Edge/physical AI is pitched as the next semiconductor demand wave after data-center AI.
insights.locator: AI will push computing from centralized

insights.claim: Quantum computing, communications and sensing are expected to create new semiconductor ecosystems around control electronics, cryogenics, photonics, specialized materials and heterogeneous integration.
insights.speaker: Richard Curtin
insights.so_what: Picks-and-shovels opportunity in quantum control and cryo electronics.

insights.claim: Expansion of space-based communications, sensing, potential space data centers such as Google Suncatcher, and transportation will require radiation-tolerant, highly reliable and energy-efficient devices.
insights.speaker: Richard Curtin
insights.so_what: Rad-hard, energy-efficient silicon is a niche positioned for growth if orbital compute materializes.

insights.claim: GlobalFoundries CEO Tim Breen will keynote the November 11, 2026 forum at the Computer History Museum on 'AI Everywhere to Quantum at Scale', followed by a panel with Quadric AI's Veerbhan Kheterpal, Mayfield's Navin Chaddha, Anderon's Dan Dechene and IQMP's Harley Johnson.
insights.speaker: Richard Curtin
insights.so_what: GlobalFoundries is publicly tying its narrative to quantum at scale — watch for quantum foundry positioning.
insights.locator: We’re pleased to have our opening keynote

insights.claim: When '2001: A Space Odyssey' was released in 1968, the smallest commercial transistor geometry was about 8,000 nm and worldwide semiconductor sales were roughly $14.5 billion in 2026 dollars.
insights.speaker: Richard Curtin
insights.so_what: Useful baseline for long-run industry scaling comparisons.

insights.claim: The author argues, half-jokingly, that Clarke's premise of machines trying to control humanity is now front-and-center daily, reflecting the industry's current struggle to rein in AI innovations.
insights.speaker: Richard Curtin
insights.so_what: Indicates AI-safety anxiety is now mainstream even in semiconductor industry marketing.
